strengths: The architecture offers a useful, technically coherent quality–efficiency tradeoff: compact viewpoint tokens exchange information globally while repeatedly accessing high-resolution image tokens through per-view cross-attention. This reduces attention costs and Gaussian counts without requiring low-resolution image inputs.

Benefits persist in matched-view comparisons. On RE10K with two views, iLRM achieves 28.65 dB versus 28.10 for GS-LRM and 27.47 for DepthSplat (Table 1). On DL3DV with 11 views, it achieves 26.99 versus 24.28 dB for DepthSplat, with lower reconstruction time (0.051 versus 0.170 seconds), memory usage (1.59 versus 6.01 GB), and one-quarter as many Gaussians (Table 3).

Evaluation covers sparse-view reconstruction, cross-dataset generalization, high-resolution inputs, and wide-coverage scenes. Table 5 demonstrates practical usefulness beyond interpolation: at 32 views, iLRM improves PSNR and SSIM over LongLRM, and its compact representation supports substantially faster subsequent optimization.

Ablations substantiate the architectural choices. Removing repeated image cross-attention, resolution decoupling, or token uplifting reduces PSNR by 0.66, 0.77, and 0.34 dB, respectively (Table 8). Mini-batch cross-attention reduces training iteration time from 1.51 to 0.94 seconds and memory from 62.5 to 39.0 GB, with a 0.31 dB loss (Table 6).

Overall, the supported architectural and empirical contribution favors acceptance. The reservations primarily limit the interpretation of novelty and the breadth of superiority claims rather than invalidate the demonstrated reconstruction benefits.
weaknesses: The claimed connection to feedback-driven optimization is stronger than the implemented mechanism supports. Equations 3–4 describe distinct transformer layers attending to fixed image tokens; intermediate Gaussians are not rendered, and reconstruction errors or gradients are not fed back. Table 8 establishes the value of repeated conditioning, but not an optimization-like refinement mechanism. Originality is therefore best understood as an effective architectural combination rather than a new learned optimization procedure.

The largest RE10K and cross-dataset gains compare four- or eight-view iLRM against two-view baselines. Additional intermediate images provide substantially more scene information, so these results do not isolate architectural improvements. Matched-view results elsewhere support the contribution, but Table 11 also changes input resolution between methods and does not fully resolve this attribution issue. Baseline training budgets are not sufficiently aligned or documented to isolate architecture from training scale.

Claims of consistently superior reconstruction quality overlook perceptual tradeoffs. At six views on DL3DV, iLRM has worse LPIPS than DepthSplat (0.168 versus 0.147, Table 3). In wide-coverage reconstruction, its feed-forward LPIPS is slightly worse than LongLRM and substantially worse than optimization-based 3D-GS (0.257 versus 0.254 and 0.213 at 32 views, Table 5), despite better PSNR and SSIM.

Scalability is improved in constants rather than fundamentally resolved: global viewpoint self-attention remains quadratic in view count, and Gaussian count still grows linearly with input views. Appendix B also constrains Gaussian positions around viewpoint rays, so the representation is decoupled from image resolution but remains viewpoint-grid-based. Experiments reaching 32 views do not establish feasibility at the 200-view scale used in the motivation.

Reproducibility has specific gaps despite substantial implementation detail. The structured mini-batch sampling schedule across layers and treatment of unselected tokens are not specified precisely; high-resolution finetuning schedules are incomplete; and Appendix B reports an unusual AdamW beta2 of 0.095 without clarification. Table 6's GFLOPs are only for a single per-view cross-attention operation excluding token uplifting, rather than the complete model, which should be explicit in the table.

strengths: The paper provides a useful architectural contribution for feed-forward scene reconstruction: compact viewpoint tokens exchange information globally while repeatedly accessing high-resolution images through per-view cross-attention. This separates output density from input resolution and produces a convincing quality–efficiency tradeoff.

The gains are supported by matched-view comparisons, not solely by providing additional images. On RE10K, the two-view model achieves 28.65 dB versus 27.47 for DepthSplat and 28.10 for GS-LRM (Table 1). At six views on DL3DV, it improves PSNR from DepthSplat's 24.19 to 25.60 while reducing reconstruction time from 0.102 to 0.031 seconds, memory from 3.55 to 1.40 GB, and Gaussian count by fourfold (Table 3).

Evaluation includes cross-dataset transfer, high-resolution inputs, and wide-coverage reconstruction. The equal-two-view transfer results improve PSNR and SSIM on both ACID and DL3DV (Table 2). Comparisons with LongLRM also demonstrate practical value: ten epochs of refinement take 7 rather than 37 seconds, with slightly better reconstruction metrics (Table 5).

The ablations substantiate the main design choices. Repeated image access, high-resolution guidance, and token uplifting each improve performance (Table 8). Mini-batch cross-attention reduces training iteration time from 1.51 to 0.94 seconds and memory from 62.5 to 39.0 GB for a 0.31 dB PSNR reduction (Table 6). Together, these results support weak acceptance despite reservations about framing and experimental attribution.
weaknesses: The optimization-inspired framing overstates what is demonstrated. Equations (3)–(4) describe a stack of independently parameterized attention blocks; there is no intermediate rendering, reconstruction-error feedback, or explicit Gaussian update. Table 8 establishes the benefit of repeated image conditioning, but does not establish optimization-like behavior. Similarly, increasing network depth also increases parameter count (Table 7), so that experiment does not isolate additional refinement steps. The supported novelty is principally architectural.

The largest RE10K and transfer improvements compare four- or eight-view predictions against two-view baselines. Additional images sampled between the endpoints supply substantial geometric and appearance information, even though target frames are excluded. These results demonstrate the usefulness of accommodating more inputs but cannot isolate architectural superiority. The matched-view results mitigate this concern; the equal-Gaussian comparison in Table 11 is also informative but changes input resolution and training configurations.

Claims of consistently superior reconstruction quality need qualification. At six views on DL3DV, LPIPS is worse than DepthSplat's (0.168 versus 0.147). In wide-coverage inference, LPIPS is slightly worse than LongLRM's at both view counts and substantially worse than optimization-based methods at 32 views (Table 5). The evidence supports strong PSNR, SSIM, and efficiency results, rather than uniform perceptual superiority.

Scalability and representation independence remain partial. Global self-attention is still quadratic in the total viewpoint-token count, and Equation (1) makes Gaussian count proportional to the number of input views. Appendix B also constrains Gaussian positions through viewpoint-grid offsets. Thus, the method decouples input resolution from output density but does not eliminate view-dependent representation growth. The paper acknowledges the attention bottleneck, and evaluation extends only to 32 views.

Some implementation details remain insufficiently explicit for reproduction: the mini-batch token-selection schedule across layers, treatment of unselected tokens, and complete high-resolution training schedules are not specified clearly. Table 6's GFLOPs are only for one per-view cross-attention operation and exclude token uplifting, as explained in Appendix F; this scope should be stated directly in the table. These are reproducibility and presentation limitations rather than evidence that the measured runtime gains are invalid.

strengths: The paper makes a useful architectural contribution: compact viewpoint tokens repeatedly access high-resolution image features through per-view cross-attention, while global self-attention integrates information across views. This provides a practical way to reduce Gaussian density without discarding high-resolution visual input.

Matched-view comparisons support a strong quality–efficiency tradeoff. On RE10K, the two-view model achieves 28.65 dB versus DepthSplat’s 27.47 dB, with reconstruction times of 0.025 versus 0.065 seconds (Table 1). On DL3DV with 11 views, it achieves 26.99 versus 24.28 dB while using roughly one-quarter as many Gaussians and substantially less inference memory (Table 3).

Evaluation covers two training datasets, cross-dataset transfer, multiple resolutions, and wide-coverage reconstruction. Table 5 also demonstrates practical usefulness as an initialization for subsequent optimization: 10-epoch refinement takes 7 seconds versus LongLRM’s 37 seconds, with slightly better reported quality.

The ablations provide meaningful support for the design. Repeated image access, resolution decoupling, and token uplifting each improve reconstruction (Table 8); supplementary experiments examine initialization and global versus per-view cross-attention. Mini-batch attention reduces training iteration time from 1.51 to 0.94 seconds with a 0.31 dB PSNR decrease (Table 6). Together, these results favor acceptance despite the qualifications below.
weaknesses: The central optimization-inspired framing exceeds what is demonstrated. Equations 3–4 describe distinct transformer layers attending to fixed image features; there is no intermediate rendering, reconstruction-error feedback, or explicit Gaussian update. Table 8 supports repeated image conditioning, but does not establish optimization-like behavior. Likewise, increasing depth also increases parameter count, so Table 7 cannot isolate the benefit of additional refinement steps. The strongest contribution is the efficient architecture rather than a demonstrated learned optimizer.

Several prominent improvements combine architectural changes with additional observations. The four- and eight-view RE10K variants receive intermediate images unavailable to the two-view baselines, which can substantially simplify novel-view synthesis. These are useful practical comparisons, but their gains cannot be attributed entirely to the architecture. Matched-view results elsewhere mitigate this concern; training-budget differences remain less clearly controlled.

Claims of consistently superior reconstruction quality need qualification. At six views on DL3DV, LPIPS is worse than DepthSplat’s despite better PSNR and SSIM (0.168 versus 0.147, Table 3). In the 32-view wide-coverage setting, feed-forward LPIPS is worse than both LongLRM and optimized 3D-GS (0.257 versus 0.254 and 0.213, Table 5). The evidence supports a favorable tradeoff, rather than uniform fidelity superiority.

Scalability and decoupling are partial. Equation 1 still allocates Gaussians in proportion to input-view count, and global viewpoint self-attention remains quadratic in that count. Appendix B also retains a viewpoint-grid parameterization with bounded spatial offsets. Experiments up to 32 views support improved operating efficiency, but do not establish scalability to the much larger scene configurations motivating the introduction.

Reproducibility is helped by substantial implementation detail, but some consequential settings remain underspecified: the exact scheduling of structured mini-batch attention across layers, the high-resolution DL3DV fine-tuning schedule, and the settings for post-inference Gaussian optimization. Also, Table 6’s GFLOPs measure only one per-view cross-attention operation and exclude token uplifting, rather than measuring the complete model. These are correctable reporting limitations; the measured runtime and memory results remain valuable.

strengths: The paper presents a useful architecture for efficient feed-forward scene reconstruction: compact viewpoint tokens receive high-resolution image evidence through per-view cross-attention and exchange information through global self-attention. The resulting quality–efficiency tradeoff supports acceptance despite reservations about the optimization interpretation.

Gains hold under matched input-view counts. On two-view RE10K, iLRM achieves 28.65 dB versus 28.10 for GS-LRM and 27.47 for DepthSplat (Table 1). On six-view DL3DV, it achieves 25.60 versus 24.19 dB for DepthSplat, with lower reported latency and memory and four times fewer Gaussians, although LPIPS is worse (Table 3).

The high-resolution evaluation demonstrates practical value. At 32 views, iLRM improves over Long-LRM from 23.97 to 24.30 dB while reducing inference time from 0.84 to 0.53 seconds (Table 5). Additional evaluation splits, unseen view counts, and faster post-prediction optimization strengthen this evidence.

Ablations support the architectural choices. Repeated image cross-attention, resolution decoupling, and token uplifting each improve reconstruction (Table 7). Quarter cross-attention reduces training iteration time from 1.51 to 0.94 seconds and memory from 62.5 to 39.0 GB at a 0.31 dB cost (Table 8).

The supplement provides substantial implementation and evaluation detail, including optimization settings, camera normalization, Gaussian parameterization, geometry experiments, and pose perturbation tests. This goes meaningfully beyond novel-view image metrics alone.
weaknesses: The optimization interpretation exceeds the demonstrated mechanism. The network uses distinct parameters across layers, static image features, and a final Gaussian decoder; it does not compute reconstruction feedback or gradients during these updates. Section 3.2 introduces an implicit energy without establishing that the learned updates approximate its gradient. Table 7 supports repeated image conditioning, and attention visualizations suggest correspondence refinement, but neither establishes an optimization process. The originality is more convincingly architectural than a new learned optimizer.

The strongest RE10K gains use four or eight input views against predominantly two-view baselines, so those gains cannot be attributed solely to architecture. Matched-view results remain positive, but training budgets are not systematically matched across methods. The equal-Gaussian comparison in Table 17 also gives iLRM higher-resolution image evidence, making it useful as a practical tradeoff comparison rather than a controlled architectural comparison.

Scalability improves substantially in constants but remains quadratic in the total number of viewpoint tokens, and Gaussian count still grows linearly with input views. Table 15 shows inference increasing from 0.53 seconds at 32 views to 20.92 seconds at 256 views; reconstruction quality at these largest view counts is unreported. Thus the evidence supports improved practical capacity, rather than removal of the many-view bottleneck.

Broad superiority claims need qualification. In Table 13, zero-shot PSNR on Tanks&Temples and Mip-NeRF360 is essentially tied with Long-LRM, while LPIPS is worse. The claim of quality comparable to optimization-based 3D-GS is strongest for PSNR on one DL3DV setting: Table 5 still shows a substantial LPIPS gap, 0.256 versus 0.191, and Table 10 shows a 1.16 dB PSNR deficit.

Geometry evidence is encouraging but has methodological limits. Table 11 measures agreement with predicted MoGe-2 depth rather than ground truth, as acknowledged. Table 12 downsamples ground-truth pointmaps specifically for iLRM and omits sufficient detail about scene selection, alignment, and metric units to fully assess comparability; its 32-view NRGBD Chamfer distance also favors Long-LRM.

Some reproducibility details remain ambiguous: the layer-wise selection schedule for mini-batch cross-attention, the mapping from patch tokens to per-pixel Gaussian outputs, and the exact training schedule for the Long-LRM comparison are not fully specified. Table 8's GFLOPs describe only a single per-view cross-attention operation without token uplifting, rather than total model computation; that scope should be explicit in the table.

strengths: The paper provides a useful architectural contribution: compact viewpoint tokens receive high-resolution image evidence through per-view cross-attention and exchange information through global self-attention. This offers a technically plausible way to reduce computation and Gaussian density while retaining reconstruction quality. The supported practical contribution favors acceptance despite reservations about its optimization-inspired framing.

Improvements hold in matched-input comparisons, not only when additional views are supplied. On two-view RE10K, Table 1 reports 28.65 dB versus 28.10 for GS-LRM and 27.47 for DepthSplat. On six-view DL3DV, Table 3 reports 25.60 versus 24.19 dB for DepthSplat, with inference reduced from 0.102 to 0.031 seconds and memory from 3.55 to 1.40 GB, although LPIPS is worse.

The wide-coverage results demonstrate practical usefulness. At 32 views, Table 5 improves over Long-LRM from 23.97 to 24.30 dB while reducing inference from 0.84 to 0.53 seconds and generating four times fewer Gaussians. Post-prediction optimization also achieves slightly better quality in substantially less time.

The ablations substantiate the main engineering choices. Table 7 measures benefits from repeated image cross-attention, resolution decoupling, and token uplifting. Table 9 supports separating per-view image interaction from global viewpoint interaction. Table 8 demonstrates a meaningful training tradeoff: quarter cross-attention reduces iteration time from 1.51 to 0.94 seconds and memory from 62.5 to 39.0 GB at a 0.31 dB PSNR cost.

Evaluation is reasonably broad, including cross-dataset transfer, unseen view counts, geometry measurements, pose perturbations, and post-prediction optimization. The supplement supplies substantial architectural, optimizer, training, and camera-normalization details, while the limitations section acknowledges quadratic self-attention and dependence on accurate poses.
weaknesses: The claimed connection to feedback-driven optimization is substantially stronger than the evidence establishes. The model uses separately parameterized transformer layers, static image tokens, and final-layer Gaussian decoding; it does not compute intermediate rendering errors or gradients. The implicit-energy gradient-descent interpretation is neither derived nor validated. Table 7 supports repeated conditioning on image evidence, while increasing both depth and parameter count in Table 6 does not establish optimization-like refinement. This limits the conceptual novelty, although it does not invalidate the architecture.

Representation decoupling and scalability are partial. Gaussian count remains proportional to the number of input views, and Appendix A constrains Gaussian positions through viewpoint pixels with bounded image-plane offsets. Global viewpoint self-attention remains quadratic in view count. Table 15 illustrates the resulting limit: inference rises from 0.53 seconds at 32 views to 20.92 seconds at 256 views, and the speed advantage over Long-LRM narrows at larger comparable counts.

Some comparisons do not isolate architectural gains. The four- and eight-view RE10K results provide additional observations unavailable to two-view baselines. Table 17 controls Gaussian count by reducing baseline input resolution, so it demonstrates a useful system tradeoff rather than a controlled comparison under identical image evidence. The two-view model also receives substantial training on eight H100 GPUs for 200,000 iterations, without a matched-training-budget comparison. These qualifications temper causal attribution but do not erase the matched-view results.

Claims of consistently superior quality and comparability to optimization-based reconstruction need qualification. Six-view DL3DV LPIPS is worse than DepthSplat's, and Table 13 shows essentially tied zero-shot PSNR but worse LPIPS than Long-LRM on Tanks&Temples and Mip-NeRF360. In Table 5, near-matching 3D-GS PSNR at 32 views still accompanies appreciably worse LPIPS, 0.256 versus 0.191.

The geometry evidence has protocol limitations. Table 11 measures agreement with monocular pseudo-depth rather than ground truth. Table 12 downscales ground-truth pointmaps specifically for iLRM, leaving ambiguity about whether both methods are evaluated against equivalent references; alignment and metric units are insufficiently specified. Moreover, 32-view NRGBD Chamfer distance is worse than Long-LRM's. These results support a qualified geometry claim rather than uniformly better geometric reconstruction.

strengths: The paper provides a useful architectural contribution to feed-forward scene reconstruction: compact viewpoint tokens receive high-resolution image information through per-view cross-attention and exchange information through global self-attention. This enables explicit Gaussian scenes with a favorable quality–efficiency tradeoff. The empirical contribution supports weak acceptance despite reservations about the optimization interpretation.

Improvements hold in matched-view comparisons. On two-view RE10K, iLRM achieves 28.65 dB versus 28.10 for GS-LRM and 27.47 for DepthSplat (Table 1). On six-view DL3DV, it achieves 25.60 versus 24.19 dB for DepthSplat, using four times fewer Gaussians, 0.031 versus 0.102 seconds, and 1.40 versus 3.55 GB (Table 3), although LPIPS is worse.

The wide-coverage experiments demonstrate practical value beyond sparse-view reconstruction. With 32 views, iLRM improves over Long-LRM from 23.97 to 24.30 dB while reducing inference time from 0.84 to 0.53 seconds (Table 5). Its compact output also supports faster subsequent optimization: 4.5 versus 11 seconds for ten epochs, with slightly better rendering metrics.

The ablations substantiate the principal design choices. Repeated image cross-attention, resolution decoupling, and token uplifting each improve reconstruction (Table 7). Quarter cross-attention reduces training iteration time from 1.51 to 0.94 seconds and memory from 62.5 to 39.0 GB, with a 0.31 dB reduction (Table 8). These measurements support a meaningful engineering contribution.

Evaluation is extensive, including cross-dataset transfer, unseen view counts, pose perturbations, geometry measurements, and post-prediction optimization. Architectural figures and supplementary optimizer, normalization, and training details make the overall approach reasonably understandable and reproducible.
weaknesses: The feedback-driven optimization interpretation is stronger than the evidence establishes. The model uses distinct parameters across layers, fixed image features, and only a final Gaussian decoding; it does not measure intermediate rendering errors or demonstrate descent on an objective. Table 7 supports repeated image conditioning, but neither that ablation nor selected attention visualizations establishes gradient-like updates. The demonstrated novelty is primarily architectural rather than a new learned optimization procedure.

Decoupling is partial: Equation 1 still generates N times Hv times Wv Gaussians, and Appendix A anchors their positions to viewpoint pixels with bounded offsets. Global self-attention remains quadratic in the number of viewpoint tokens. The paper acknowledges this bottleneck, and Table 15 shows latency rising from 0.53 seconds at 32 views to 20.92 seconds at 256 views. The evidence supports reduced computational constants and resolution flexibility, rather than eliminating view-dependent redundancy or quadratic scaling.

Some headline improvements mix architectural gains with additional observations or training resources. The four- and eight-view results in Tables 1–2 use more input evidence than the two-view baselines. Appendix A also reports substantial, configuration-dependent training budgets without establishing matched training compute across methods. The matched-view comparisons remain valuable, but the larger gains cannot be attributed solely to the proposed architecture.

Claims of consistently superior reconstruction quality need qualification. Six-view DL3DV LPIPS is worse than DepthSplat despite higher PSNR (Table 3). On Tanks&Temples and Mip-NeRF360, zero-shot PSNR essentially matches Long-LRM while LPIPS is worse (Table 13). Likewise, being close to optimized 3D-GS in PSNR on the main DL3DV benchmark does not imply comparable perceptual quality: LPIPS is 0.256 versus 0.191 (Table 5).

The geometry evidence has methodological limitations. MoGe-2 agreement is appropriately described as a proxy, but the ground-truth geometry evaluation downsamples reference pointmaps specifically for iLRM without clearly establishing a common evaluation reference, coordinate units, or alignment protocol (Table 12). Its 32-view NRGBD Chamfer distance is also worse than Long-LRM. These issues limit the strength of the claimed geometric advantage, although they do not negate the rendering and efficiency results.
